thread:
mike: Heads-up — APAC rack-3 started spiking tail latency for some dedicated slices this morning. Tenants on "dedicated" pools still saw 95p token latency jump ~2.3x for short windows. Suspect NIC resets + egress microbursts causing KV-cache churn.

sanjay: Yup saw that. Kernel logs show a bunch of VF reset lines around 07:12 UTC. Quick snippet: ```
Mar 12 07:11:59 node-3 kernel: ixgbevf 0000:08:00.1: VF reset request
Mar 12 07:12:00 node-3 kernel: ixgbevf 0000:08:00.1: Link status changed - reset
Mar 12 07:12:00 node-3 infra-proxy: shard-evict key=kvcache:tenant:42
```

mike: exactly — the probe traces line up: when VF reset happens we see a blip of dropped packets then ~10s of KV scavenges. Dedicated slices should shield that, but eviction + rewarm hurt token latency.

elaine: Any idea if this is driver-level (ixgbevf) or something in our sidecar proxy queueing?

sanjay: Driver + NIC firmware pattern. We've had similar earlier but was masked by warm-pool headroom. This time headroom exhausted because of aggressive fractional packing.

mike: Proposal: add a tiny per-tenant ephemeral "burstcap" reserve (e.g., 10–50MB of egress credit per-slice) that scheduler allocates at start and that the proxy can draw without triggering global KV eviction. It'd be a soft reserve that decays after idle.

jia: That sounds promising. Implementation sketch: scheduler flag `--burstcap-mb` per slice, proxy consumes from local token bucket; on underflow fallback to normal path. Simple metrics: burstcap_used, burst_fills, burst_decays.

elaine: Cost/impact? This lowers avg cluster utilization slightly. Rough calc: if we give 20MB * 5k slices = 100GB memory footprint transient -> ~2–3% effective GPU node memory if spread out. CPU/net overhead minimal.

mike: Tradeoffs: protects SLAs for customer slices but increases committed footprint. Also future-proofing for flaky NICs while infra patch rolls out. Can we canary this in eu-west edge first?

sanjay: I'll run NIC reset repro on bench farm and try burstcap proxy patch (local token bucket) — if it smooths KV churn we can nominate eu-west canary. Need infra signoff to change scheduler defaults.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026 — "APAC rack-3 microburst -> tenant KV churn". Assigned: @sanjay, @jia. :rotating_light:

jia: I'll own the canary rollout. Plan: 1) bench repro + metrics (today), 2) proxy + scheduler toggle in eu-west limited to 50 slices (tomorrow), 3) monitor 95/99 latencies + kv-evict rates for 48h, 4) if green, propose org-config to reserve 20MB by default for customer-tier "critical".

elaine: +1. Please include cost estimate in the PR description. If risk looks low I think we can flip for critical tenants. :thumbsup:

mike: Thanks. Sanjay/Jia tag me on the PR and post the canary dashboard link here when ready.

(END)
